sources.title: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner (CLF-C02) Exam Guide, Version 1.3 (October 29, 2026)
sources.note: Domains, weights, task statements, service lists and scoring transcribed from the HTML guide and its sub-pages (domains 1-4, in-scope, out-of-scope, technologies and concepts, revisions). Revisions: 1.0 2026-06-24, 1.1 2026-08-28, 1.2 2026-09-24, 1.3 2026-10-29; AWS publishes updates about a month before they reach the exam. This replaces an earlier transcription of an older CLF-C02 PDF, which used retired service names and support plans. The `scope` arrays are CONDENSED from the guide's 'Knowledge of / Skills in' bullets.

exam.name: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner
exam.passMarkNote: Official pass mark is a scaled score of 700 on a 100-1000 scale (compensatory scoring: only the overall result matters). The raw-percentage equivalent is not published, so 70% is a PROXY for display on mock results only.
exam.readinessTargetNote: Your own per-exam target for dashboard/map status (default 80%). Not a vendor figure.
exam.unscoredNote: 15 unscored questions are not identified on the real exam. Unanswered = incorrect; no penalty for guessing.

questionTypes.single: Multiple choice: 1 correct response, 3 distractors (4 options).
questionTypes.multi: Multiple response: 2 or more correct responses out of 5 or more options.

marketing.tagline: The broad map of AWS: what the cloud is, how it is secured, and how it is billed.
marketing.audience: Anyone who works near AWS and needs the vocabulary: new engineers, managers, sales and support staff, career changers.
highlights: Cloud Technology and Services is the biggest domain at 34%, so service recognition pays off most.
Security and Compliance is 30%: the shared responsibility model comes up everywhere.
No hands-on experience required, but the questions reward knowing which service fits which job.

objectives.title: Define the benefits of the AWS Cloud.
scope: Value proposition of the AWS Cloud
Benefits of global infrastructure (speed of deployment, global reach)
High availability, elasticity, agility

objectives.title: Identify design principles of the AWS Cloud.
scope: AWS Well-Architected Framework
Pillars: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, sustainability
Differences between the pillars

objectives.title: Understand the benefits of and strategies for migration to the AWS Cloud.
scope: Cloud adoption strategies
Resources that support the migration journey
AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) benefits: reduced business risk, improved ESG performance, increased revenue, increased operational efficiency
Migration strategies (e.g. database replication)

objectives.title: Understand concepts of cloud economics.
scope: Aspects of cloud economics and cost savings of moving to the cloud
Fixed vs variable costs
Costs of on-premises environments
Licensing: Bring Your Own License (BYOL) vs included licenses
Rightsizing
Benefits of automation
Economies of scale

objectives.title: Understand the AWS shared responsibility model.
scope: Components of the AWS shared responsibility model
Customer responsibilities; AWS responsibilities; shared responsibilities
How responsibilities shift by service (e.g. Amazon RDS, AWS Lambda, Amazon EC2)

objectives.title: Understand AWS Cloud security, governance, and compliance concepts.
scope: Compliance and governance concepts; where to find compliance information (AWS Artifact)
Compliance needs by geography or industry (AWS compliance); requirements that vary among services
Securing resources (Amazon Inspector, AWS Security Hub, Amazon GuardDuty, AWS Shield)
Benefits of cloud security; encryption in transit and at rest
Governance and compliance: monitoring with Amazon CloudWatch; auditing with AWS CloudTrail and AWS Config; reporting with access reports
Where to capture and locate security logs

objectives.title: Identify AWS access management capabilities.
scope: AWS IAM: users, groups, custom and managed policies, least privilege
Protecting the root user; tasks only the root user can perform; root protection methods
Authentication: MFA, AWS IAM Identity Center, cross-account IAM roles; federated identity
Access keys, password policies, credential storage (AWS Secrets Manager, AWS Systems Manager)

objectives.title: Identify components and resources for security.
scope: Security features and services (AWS WAF, AWS Firewall Manager, AWS Shield, Amazon GuardDuty)
Third-party security products in AWS Marketplace
Where security information lives: AWS Knowledge Center, AWS Security Center, AWS Security Blog
AWS Trusted Advisor for identifying security issues

objectives.title: Define methods of deploying and operating in the AWS Cloud.
scope: Ways to provision, operate and access AWS: APIs, SDKs, CLI, AWS Management Console, infrastructure as code
One-time operations vs repeatable processes
Deployment models: cloud, hybrid, on-premises

objectives.title: Define the AWS global infrastructure.
scope: Regions, Availability Zones and edge locations, and how they relate
High availability with multiple Availability Zones; AZs do not share single points of failure
When to use multiple Regions (disaster recovery, business continuity, low latency for end users, data sovereignty)
Benefits of edge locations

objectives.title: Identify AWS compute services.
scope: EC2 instance types (e.g. compute optimized, storage optimized)
Containers: Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS
Serverless compute: AWS Fargate, AWS Lambda
Auto scaling provides elasticity
Purpose of load balancers

objectives.title: Identify AWS database services.
scope: EC2-hosted vs AWS managed databases
Relational: Amazon RDS, Amazon Aurora
NoSQL: Amazon DynamoDB
Memory-based: Amazon ElastiCache
Database migration: AWS DMS, AWS SCT

objectives.title: Identify AWS network services.
scope: VPC components (subnets, gateways)
VPC security: network ACLs, security groups, Amazon Inspector
Purpose of Amazon Route 53
Connectivity to AWS: AWS VPN, AWS Direct Connect

objectives.title: Identify AWS storage services.
scope: Uses of object storage; Amazon S3 storage classes
Block storage: Amazon EBS, instance store
File services: Amazon EFS, Amazon FSx
Cached file systems: AWS Storage Gateway
Lifecycle policies
AWS Backup

objectives.title: Identify AWS artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) services and analytics services.
scope: AI/ML services and their tasks (e.g. Amazon SageMaker AI, Amazon Lex)
Analytics services (e.g. Amazon Athena, Amazon Kinesis, AWS Glue, Amazon Quick)

objectives.title: Identify services from other in-scope AWS service categories.
scope: Messaging, alerts and notifications: Amazon EventBridge, Amazon SNS, Amazon SQS
Business applications: Amazon Connect, Amazon SES
Business support: AWS Support
Developer tools to develop, deploy and troubleshoot: AWS CodeBuild, AWS CodePipeline, AWS X-Ray
End-user computing: Amazon AppStream 2.0, Amazon WorkSpaces, Amazon WorkSpaces Secure Browser
Frontend web and mobile: AWS Amplify
IoT: AWS IoT Core

objectives.title: Compare AWS pricing models.
scope: Compute purchasing options: On-Demand, Reserved Instances, Spot Instances, Savings Plans, Dedicated Hosts, Dedicated Instances, Capacity Reservations
Reserved Instance flexibility and behavior in AWS Organizations
Incoming and outgoing data transfer costs (Region to Region, within a Region)
Pricing for storage options and tiers

objectives.title: Understand resources for billing, budget, and cost management.
scope: Uses of AWS Budgets and AWS Cost Explorer
AWS Pricing Calculator
AWS Organizations consolidated billing and cost allocation
Cost allocation tags and billing reports (AWS Cost and Usage Report)
Billing support and pricing information

objectives.title: Identify AWS technical resources and AWS Support options.
scope: Whitepapers, blogs and documentation on official AWS websites
Technical resources: AWS Prescriptive Guidance, AWS Knowledge Center, AWS re:Post
AWS Support options: customer service and communities, Basic Support, AWS Business Support+, AWS Enterprise Support, AWS Unified Operations; AWS Support Center
AWS Trusted Advisor, AWS Health Dashboard, AWS Health API
AWS Trust and Safety team (reporting abuse)
AWS Partners and the AWS Partner Network (ISVs, system integrators); partner benefits; AWS Marketplace
AWS Professional Services, AWS solutions architects
